address: 400 7th Street, S.W. Room PL401, Washington D.C. 20590
subject: COMMENTS CONCERNING SMOKING IN AIRPORTS

comments.title: PATH ONLY
comments.description: DOT has suggested that guaranteeing passengers sensitive to tobacco smoke "a path of access from the terminal entrance to the aircraft free from exposure to tobacco smoke," perhaps by using "an enclosed cart that took the passenger through the airport without exposure to smoke," would provide sufficient protection.
comments.question: Do you agree or disagree? Why?
comments.response: I agree that providing a smoke-free path from the terminal entrance to the aircraft is important for protecting passengers sensitive to tobacco smoke. However, relying solely on an enclosed cart may not be sufficient for all travelers, as it could be inconvenient and may not cover all exposure points. A comprehensive smoke-free policy throughout the terminal would better ensure the health and comfort of all passengers.

comments.title: OTHER AREAS
comments.description: Are there other areas of the airport terminal that passengers – including those sensitive to tobacco smoke – frequently must use while traveling, and where they therefore need protection from exposure to tobacco smoke (e.g. restrooms, telephones, eating areas, baggage claim, news stands and other stores, ticket counters, etc.)?
comments.question: If yes, explain why these areas are important to travelers, and what smoking restrictions (if any) should be adopted.
comments.response: Yes, other areas such as restrooms, eating areas, baggage claim, ticket counters, and stores are frequently used by all passengers and should be smoke-free to protect everyone from secondhand smoke exposure. Smoking restrictions should include a complete ban on smoking inside the terminal building, with designated smoking areas located outside and away from entrances to minimize smoke infiltration.
